question: A normal chest radiograph in a child with a convincing history of foreign body aspiration effectively rules out the diagnosis and bronchoscopy is not needed.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. The majority of aspirated foreign bodies are radiolucent and will not appear on CXR. A normal film never clears a convincing choking history — bronchoscopy is still indicated.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That is correct — this statement is FALSE. Most aspirated foreign bodies are radiolucent (peanuts, plastic). A normal CXR does not exclude aspiration; bronchoscopy is diagnostic and therapeutic when the history is compelling.
